newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour favours "pay up" deterrent to gazumping.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour favours "pay up" deterrent to gazumping.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party said on Tuesday it was determined to tackle the problem of "gazumping" in house sales and favoured a scheme under which sellers would compensate would-be buyers who suffer from it.
Environment spokesman Frank Dobson published a consultation paper setting out a series of options for dealing with the problem of sellers who jilt buyers and accept a higher offer.
But he said the one he favoured would force such sellers to compensate the jilted buyers for the legal fees they had incurred on a planned purchase which came to nothing.
This, the paper said, offers the "most sensible and practical" way forward.
However Dobson said he would consult with the public and the estate agency profession before adopting the idea as policy.
"The process of buying a house is one of the most stressful things that a family can encounter. So the Government should try to have in place a system which keeps stress to a minimum," Dobson said.
"We are determined to act against gazumping." -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
